response:
Diagnosis driving this generation. Generation 7 delivered a decisive result: the *dynamics* of capital-return policy, interacted with cross-sectional cheapness, dominate everything built from policy levels. Improving Capital Return Trajectory earned FF5 alpha 0.038 with t 3.76 (fmb 2.43, coverage 0.094) and Cardinal Payout Deviation From Own Norm earned 0.036 with t 3.27 at full coverage 0.112 and the best Sharpe in the family (0.396) — both far beyond anything the level-based enterprise-value family produced (0.014, t 1.42) and beyond the accrual-credibility branch (0.023, t 2.22). Three lessons follow. First, the informative object is a *change in policy*, not the size of the policy: FF5 has no factor for "this firm is becoming more shareholder-oriented," so the abnormal return survives. Second, cardinal within-firm deviation works too, contradicting the prior that lumpy annual flows defeat cardinal measures — so both the ordinal and cardinal branches are live. Third, credibility weighting no longer adds once the dynamic measure is used (0.030 → 0.023 when stacked), so this generation drops that branch and spends its slots refining the trajectory mechanism: a more robust regime-shift estimator, a two-sided valuation weighting, a fully within-firm version, a component test, a noise-standardized version, and a purge of the earnings cycle from the trajectory.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Payout Regime Shift When Cheap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3), LAG(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 3), 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: A durable change in capital-allocation policy is best measured as the gap between what a firm has returned on average over the last three years and what it returned on average over the three years before that; a cheap firm whose sustained payout level has stepped up between those regimes has undergone a real change in management behavior rather than experiencing a single unusual year.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The five-observation OLS trend that produced alpha 0.038 is statistically fragile — one outlier year can dominate its slope — and comparing two three-year averages estimates the same policy-shift concept using six years of information with far more robustness to lumpy repurchase timing. This is a different estimator of the winning economic object, not a horizon tweak, and it should raise the cross-sectional slope (currently only 2.43) if trend noise is what has been diluting it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Two Sided Payout Trajectory
EXPRESSION: ADD(MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), ADD(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1), ABS(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1)))), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc)))), SUB(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1), ABS(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: An improving capital-return trajectory is bullish precisely where the shares are cheap, but a deteriorating trajectory — a firm turning steadily from returning capital to consuming it — is most damaging where the shares are expensive, because that is the firm whose premium depends on growth it must now fund externally.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The current trajectory signal weights both improving and deteriorating firms by cheapness, so its short leg is cheap firms with worsening policy, whereas the economic story assigns the short leg to expensive firms; the positive- and negative-part decomposition lets each side carry the valuation weight the mechanism requires. This same decomposition previously produced the archive's best raw Sharpe when applied to payout levels, so pairing it with the measurement that produces the best alpha is the natural consolidation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Own Multiple And Own Trajectory
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc)), 5), WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The strongest evidence of a management team acting on private information is a firm that is cheap relative to its own recent valuation history while its capital-return policy has been steadily improving — the market has not repriced the business even though the firm has been progressively handing capital back.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Making both legs within-firm previously lifted alpha from 0.014 to 0.028 when applied to payout position, and the trend leg is the strongest financing measurement found, so this tests whether the two orthogonalizing choices compound rather than overlap. If it beats the industry-ranked version, the conclusion is that essentially all of this family's abnormal return lives in firm-specific state changes that no cross-sectional factor can span.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Shareholder Payout Trajectory When Cheap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at), 5), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The trajectory that carries information is the one management directly controls — dividends plus repurchases net of share sales — whereas the debt-issuance component of the flow moves with refinancing calendars and credit conditions and should add noise rather than signal to a multi-year policy trend.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a component test of the winning signal with a clear economic prediction: if the shareholder-only trajectory matches or beats alpha 0.038, the mechanism is managerial payout policy, and if it deteriorates, the mechanism is genuinely about total claim contraction including deleveraging. The earlier level-based version of this ablation failed, but under a trend measurement the debt flows enter very differently, so the earlier result does not settle the question.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Noise Scaled Payout Trajectory When Cheap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(RATIO(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: A given slope in capital return means something different at a firm whose financing is normally steady than at one that swings violently every year: only a trend that is large relative to the firm's own financing variability represents a deliberate policy change rather than the visual impression left by noise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This reorders firms by the signal-to-noise ratio of their policy shift rather than by its raw slope, which should promote the steady compounders whose modest but reliable trends the raw measure buries beneath erratic firms with one large swing. Because the reordering is driven by a firm's own historical dispersion, it stays inside the factor-orthogonal within-firm space where this family's alpha has been found.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Payout Trajectory Beyond Earnings Trajectory
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), WINSOR(SUB(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), TREND(RATIO(ebitda, at), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Payout naturally rises when profitability rises, so the discretionary component of an improving capital-return trajectory is the part that exceeds the trajectory of the firm's own operating profitability: a cheap firm returning progressively more while its margins are flat has genuinely reallocated capital toward shareholders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The position-based version of this idea produced alpha 0.020 with t 1.83, which is encouraging but was built on the weaker ordinal measurement; applying the same purge to the trend measurement that scored 0.038 tests whether removing the earnings cycle sharpens or merely subtracts from the winning signal. It also directly addresses the concern that the trajectory family could be an indirect profitability-recovery bet that RMW would eventually absorb.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Payout Regime Shift When Cheap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The archive already contains two highly correlated estimators of exactly this "policy shift" object at the same valuation conditioning — the 5-year OLS trend (alpha 0.038, t 3.76) and current-level-minus-5yr-MA (alpha 0.036, t 3.27) — so a three-year-versus-lagged-three-year average difference is a third smoothing of the same construct and is very likely to be a cosmetic estimator variant rather than new economic information.

---CRITIQUE Two Sided Payout Trajectory---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The positive/negative-part decomposition is correctly constructed (ADD(x,ABS(x)) isolates improvers weighted by cheapness, SUB(x,ABS(x)) isolates deteriorators weighted by richness) and the expected positive sign follows, but the identical decomposition applied to payout levels already underperformed the simple conditional version (alpha 0.010, t 1.12), so the prior that the short-leg re-weighting helps is weak.

---CRITIQUE Own Multiple And Own Trajectory---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Combining the two orthogonalizations that each independently improved alpha (within-firm valuation ranking and the trend-measured financing leg) is a coherent test of whether they compound or overlap, though there is a real risk that TS_RANK of the EV multiple mostly picks up the same firm-specific state that a rising payout trend already encodes, making the two legs mechanically correlated.

---CRITIQUE Shareholder Payout Trajectory When Cheap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A clean single-component ablation of the winning signal with a pre-stated interpretive fork in either direction, which is legitimate mechanism testing even if it is low-ambition and its most likely outcome is a modest degradation that merely confirms the debt leg contributes.

---CRITIQUE Noise Scaled Payout Trajectory When Cheap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Dividing a 5-year slope by the 5-year volatility of the same series is numerically unstable — firms with near-zero financing variability (many of them precisely the inactive, uninformative ones) produce explosive ratios that WINSOR at 1% will not adequately tame, and the numerator is itself a component of the denominator, so the ranking risks being driven by degenerate low-dispersion cases rather than by genuine policy conviction.

---CRITIQUE Payout Trajectory Beyond Earnings Trajectory---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Purging the profitability cycle from the trajectory directly addresses the legitimate concern that this family is an RMW-spanned recovery bet, but the two raw slopes are differenced without standardization and EBITDA/assets trends are typically far larger in magnitude than net-payout/assets trends, so the composite may end up ranking primarily on declining profitability rather than on discretionary payout expansion.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Steady Deleveraging At Cheap Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc))), NEG(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), at), 5), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The trajectory that matters for a cheap firm may be on the liability side rather than the payout side: a company that has reduced its net debt burden year after year is steadily transferring enterprise value from creditors to shareholders and lowering the risk that forced the discount, whereas a cheap firm whose net debt has been climbing for five years is on a path toward distress regardless of what it currently pays out.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This applies the trajectory discovery to a genuinely different economic object — the multi-year path of the net debt *stock* rather than the annual capital-return *flow* — so it is not a third estimator of the same construct but a test of whether the mechanism is shareholder-oriented policy or balance-sheet repair. Because it uses only balance-sheet items it needs no cash-flow-statement financing data, giving it a coverage profile and a failure mode independent of the payout-trend family.
---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Compressing Multiple With Rising Payout
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), dltt), che), dlc)), 5)), WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The sharpest mispricing arises when the market and management have been moving in opposite directions for years: the multiple has been compressing — the enterprise earnings yield rising — at the same time as the firm has been steadily increasing the capital it returns, so the price is falling relative to fundamentals precisely while insiders commit more cash to buying the business back.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the unstable slope-over-volatility ratio with a second trend rather than a division, so there is no small-denominator degeneracy, and it makes both legs dynamic — a divergence-of-trajectories interaction that no archive signal has tested, since every prior version paired a static valuation level with a dynamic financing measure. The nonnegative rank weight on the multiple-compression trend preserves the sign structure, keeping rising-payout firms in the long leg and firms cutting payout into a re-rating in the short leg.
